identity.title: SVRG and Beyond via Posterior Correction

problem.claim: The work examines how SVRG and its variants can be understood and extended through Bayesian posterior correction.

gap.claim: The authors state that SVRG had not previously been connected to a Bayesian method at a fundamental level.

contributions.claim: Shows that SVRG is recoverable as a special case of posterior correction with isotropic-Gaussian posteriors.
Derives SVRG extensions using more flexible exponential-family posteriors, including a Newton-like variant with Hessian corrections and an Adam-like extension intended to scale to large problems.

stated_novelty.claim: The authors state that this is the first work to connect SVRG to Bayes and use that connection to speed up training.

author_reported_evidence.claim: The authors report the theoretical recovery of SVRG from posterior correction under isotropic-Gaussian posteriors.
The authors report two derived Gaussian-family extensions: a Newton-like method with new Hessian corrections and an Adam-like method intended for large problems.

narrative_sequence.summary: SVRG and related methods use gradient corrections to accelerate training.
The authors identify the absence of a fundamental Bayesian connection for these methods.
They connect SVRG to posterior correction and recover it under isotropic-Gaussian posteriors.
More flexible exponential-family posteriors yield Newton-like and Adam-like SVRG extensions.

source_observation.claim: The abstract frames algorithmic extensions as consequences of changing the posterior family, after first deriving a known method as a special case.

lessons.interpretation: A unifying derivation can make extensions feel systematic rather than ad hoc.
lessons.application: When proposing variants, first identify a broader formal mechanism that recovers the baseline, then state which structural choice produces each variant.
lessons.exception: This framing may be unsuitable when no credible unifying mechanism or formal recovery of the baseline is available.

unknowns: The abstract provides no experimental results, datasets, quantitative comparisons, or details supporting the claimed scalability of the Adam-like extension.
It does not specify the exact posterior-correction formulation, Hessian corrections, or conditions under which the derivations hold.
